nothing_derived_rule: Every value in this file is the publishing host's own, in the host's own unit, under the host's own identifier. The only arithmetic is `m` — great-circle metres between two published coordinates. There is no reading, no band, no threshold and no verdict here; the readings arrive live and the estimate is the app's own, on the card, with its inputs shown.
distance_rule: Every resolution carries the metres from the entry point to the instrument, and every surface that prints a reading prints that distance beside it. A spot with no instrument inside the stated radius carries NO resolution for that catalogue — never a distant one presented as a local reading.

method.radius_rule: A CIRCLE, measured in metres on a sphere of radius 6,371,008.8 m, and not a box in degrees: one degree of longitude is 94 km at the south end of this coast and 83 km at the north, so a degree window cannot make an absence sentence that names kilometres true at both ends.
method.tie_rule: Ties break on the catalogue's own order; two equidistant instruments is not a coin this lane calls.
method.catalogue_rule: Only catalogue rows some entry point actually resolved to are carried. The full catalogues read on this day were 26 CDIP stations, 11594 MOP points and 14 IOOS shore stations; carrying the MOP catalogue whole would add about ten thousand points no spot in this dataset is nearest to.

mop.what_it_is: A MODEL, not an instrument. MOP propagates offshore wave conditions to named points along the shoreline, which is why its Hs is closer to what a diver feels than a buoy twenty kilometres out — and why every surface that prints it says 'model' rather than 'measured'.

shore_stations.selection_rule: A station is in this catalogue only if its own .das shows a turbidity variable and a position inside California. Turbidity is the gate because it is the only in-situ measurement on this coast that is about how far a diver can see.

harmonic_constants.why_it_is_bundled: So the tide state works with no signal at all. The predictions endpoint stays the source of truth whenever the phone is online; the curve computed from these constants is what the card falls back to, labelled as computed, and a test compares the two.
harmonic_constants.analysis_rule: Each station carries NOAA's own `comments` string for the analysis its constants came from. A curve from a 2007-2012 analysis is a different claim from one from this year's, and the reader is told which.

harmonic_method.datum_rule: The constants describe the tide about MEAN SEA LEVEL; NOAA's predictions, every chart and every reader work in MEAN LOWER LOW WATER. A curve is computed as (MSL - MLLW) + the harmonic sum, using the STATION'S OWN published pair. A station present in `stations` and absent from `datums` cannot produce an offline curve, and a card must say so rather than assume a separation.
harmonic_method.subordinate_rule: A subordinate station has no constants of its own. CO-OPS predicts it by shifting its reference station's highs and lows by the published time offsets (minutes) and scaling by the published height offsets. `reference_station` names the station whose constants and datums to use.
